content.comment_body: Hello, could someone assist me with static and dynamic connections? I'm attempting to network 13 [product_name] modules, with one as the master and the others as slaves. Can these settings be configured in [product_name] software?

Here’s a suggestion for connecting 13 [product_name] modules using static connections. Each module operates as a master. Module 8_8 acts as a client, collecting data from servers 8_9 and 8_13. Module 8_8 then serves as a server for the main collector, 8_1. Module 8_1 collects as a client from servers 8_2 to 8_8.
Attached is the project file related to the screenshot.

Let me clarify my system further: 1. We have 13 [product_name] modules, each with 4 digital outputs and 5 digital inputs. Any digital input will activate all 52 outputs. 2. All programming will reside in the master module, while the others serve as slaves. 3. How can these be configured dynamically on the network, since the manual indicates static connections are limited to 8? 4. Is it possible to use two master modules with distributed slaves and have communication occur only between the masters?

Each [product_name] module can handle up to 8 static connections. To network 13 modules with static connections, at least two modules must be masters. Master_1 gathers inputs from Slave_1 to Slave_6, along with input from Master_2. It then controls the outputs of Slave_1 to Slave_6 and sends a shift command to Master_2. Master_2 collects inputs from Slave_7 to Slave_11, and, following Master_1’s instructions, switches its own outputs along with those of Slave_7 to Slave_11.
Are the digital inputs push buttons or switches?
Thank you, I appreciate your assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion focused on configuring a network of 13 [product_name] modules and addressing the limitations on static connections. Users explored dynamic versus static setups, clarified programming requirements for inputs and outputs, and discussed master/slave network organization within the constraints of the software.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks the capability to connect more than eight [product_name] modules dynamically, wishes to configure master/slave roles efficiently, and wants every input to reliably trigger all outputs. They expect clear guidance on configuration within the software and better understanding of hardware and software limitations.
